extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting requirements for signatures (handwritten and S-signatures), certifications, ratification/evidence of authenticity, certified-document rules, and authorized Internet/email/video communications with the USPTO as described in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwritten signature (original) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Be an original, that is, have an original handwritten signature personally signed, in permanent dark ink or its equivalent, by that person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dark ink or equivalent permits traditional ink and newer non-liquid gel type ink technologies; dark color required so scanned black-and-white images are legible. A scanned image of a handwritten signature filed via EFS is permitted as a copy under 37 CFR 1.4(d)(1)(ii). A signature applied by an electric or mechanical typewriter directly to paper is not a handwritten signature. The original, if not submitted, should be retained as evidence of proper execution; the Office may require submission of the original if authenticity is questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwritten signature (copy) acceptance and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence may be an original handwritten signature or be a direct or indirect copy, such as a photocopy or facsimile transmission (§ 1.6(d)), of an original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy is filed, the original should be retained as evidence of authenticity. Second and further generation copies are acceptable where copies are permitted (e.g., photocopy of a fax). If authenticity is questioned, the Office may require submission of the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent practitioner handwritten signature flag
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent practitioner must indicate their design patent practitioner status by placing the word 'design' (in any format) adjacent to their handwritten signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'design' indicator must appear adjacent to the handwritten signature; this is required by 37 CFR 1.4(d)(1) as applied in the MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature definition and permitted uses
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-signature is a signature inserted between forward slash marks, but not a handwritten signature as defined by paragraph (d)(1); includes any signature made by electronic or mechanical means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-signatures may be used for correspondence filed in paper, by facsimile transmission (§ 1.6(d)), or via the USPTO patent electronic filing system as an attachment (§ 1.6(a)(4)) for patent applications, patents, reexamination, or supplemental examination proceedings. 37 CFR 1.4(d) does not authorize filing correspondence by email.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature format (characters and punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The S-signature must consist only of letters, or Arabic numerals, or both, with appropriate spaces and commas, periods, apostrophes, or hyphens for punctuation, and must be enclosed between a first single forward slash and a second single forward slash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters include English and non-English letters and text characters (e.g., Kanji). Non-text graphic characters (e.g., wingdings smiley faces) are not permitted. Example: /John P. Doe/. An S-signature composed only of punctuation (e.g., /- - -/) or question marks (e.g., /???/) is improper and may be interpreted as not bona fide. Additional forward slashes as part of the S-signature are not permitted. Presentation of just letters/numerals without enclosing slashes is treated as unsigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner registration number with S-signature
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent practitioner signing pursuant to § 1.33(b)(1) or (2) must supply their registration number either as part of the S-signature, or immediately below or adjacent to the S-signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hash (#) character may only be used as part of the S-signature when appearing before a practitioner's registration number; otherwise the hash character may not be used in an S-signature. For some filings (applicant signing as inventor), a registration number is not required and should not be supplied to avoid confusion as to the basis for signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent practitioner S-signature flag
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent practitioner must indicate their design patent practitioner status by placing the word 'design' (in any format) adjacent to the last forward slash of their S-signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to S-signatures as well as handwritten signatures; it helps identify design practitioners in filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed/typed name requirement with S-signature
rubrics_metrics.description: The signer’s name must be presented in printed or typed form preferably immediately below or adjacent the S-signature and be reasonably specific enough so that the identity of the signer can be readily recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printed/typed name may be produced by mechanical/printer means (typewriter, printer, facsimile machine). A printed/typed name in the letterhead or body is not acceptable as presentation of the S-signer's name. The printed/typed name may be inserted before or after the S-signature and need not be inserted by the S-signer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic/graphic representation of signatures via EFS
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence permitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system may be signed by a graphic representation of a handwritten signature or a graphic representation of an S-signature when submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A graphic representation of a handwritten signature may be created by using a stylus pen and/or touch-pad. Graphic representations are acceptable only when submitted via the EFS per 37 CFR 1.4(d)(3); 37 CFR 1.4(d)(3) does not apply to documents submitted in paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may insert an S-signature
rubrics_metrics.description: A person must insert his or her own S-signature using letters and/or Arabic numerals with allowed punctuation; the 'must insert his or her own signature' requirement is met by the signer directly typing their own signature using a keyboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One person (e.g., a secretary) may not type the signature of another even if directed, except where a person physically unable to use a keyboard simultaneously reviews the document and directs another to press keys to form the S-signature. Knowingly adopting another's S-signature is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial signing systems and S-signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: A signature created using a commercial signing system may be acceptable under 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2) if the signature is inserted between forward slash marks or under 37 CFR 1.4(d)(3) if the signature is a graphic representation and submitted via EFS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial signing system signatures must still meet the enclosure, character, and submission-route requirements (slashed S-signature for paper/fax, graphic representation via EFS for electronic submissions). 37 CFR 1.4(d)(3) does not apply to paper submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of S-signature use
rubrics_metrics.description: For consistency and to avoid raising doubt as to who has signed, the same S-signature should be utilized each time, with variations of the signature being avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signer should ensure indicia of identity (printed name, registration number) in the body of the document are consistent with the S-signature. Repeatedly using the same noncompliant S-signature after being required to correct it will result in the reply not being considered a bona fide attempt and will not get additional time to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script fonts prohibited except for S-signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Script fonts are not permitted for any portion of a document except the S-signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation of a typed name in a script font without the typed name being placed between the required slashes does not present proper indicia of intent to sign and will be treated as an unsigned document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications when presenting papers (11.18(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The presentation to the Office (whether by signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) of any paper by a party constitutes a certification under § 11.18(b) of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of § 11.18(b)(2) may result in imposition of sanctions under § 11.18(c); practitioners violating § 11.18(b) may also be subject to disciplinary action. This applies to Office forms and papers; no changes to certification statements on Office forms may be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification as to the signature (responsibility of inserter and submitter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person inserting a signature under 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2) or (d)(3) certifies that the inserted signature is his or her own; a person submitting a document signed by another must have a reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by that person and should retain evidence of authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable basis does not require actual knowledge but requires some reason to believe the signature is appropriate (e.g., retaining emails showing execution). Violations may result in sanctions under 37 CFR 11.18(c) and (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require ratification, confirmation, or evidence of authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require ratification, confirmation (including submission of a duplicate document with a proper signature), or evidence of authenticity of a signature where there is reasonable doubt as to authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: variations in a signature, or where the signature and the typed/printed name do not clearly identify the person. Ratification requires the ratifier to state they personally signed the previously submitted document and, if needed, submit a compliant signature format. Confirmation includes submitting a duplicate document compliantly signed where the previous signature was noncompliant. Where multiple documents require ratification, an itemized list of documents and filing dates should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission when ratification is inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of ratification, the Office may require resubmission of a properly signed duplicate document when ratification alone is inappropriate (e.g., image of the signature is of such poor quality that the Office cannot store or reproduce it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmission may be required rather than ratification when the prior image quality prevents use; resubmission should be a duplicate document with a compliant signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide attempt vs unsigned paper treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The inadvertent failure to follow the format and content of an S-signature will be treated as a bona fide attempt at a signature but the paper will be considered unsigned correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of correspondence treated as unsigned: (A) S-signature not enclosed in forward slashes, (B) S-signature composed of non-text graphic characters, (C) S-signature not a name and no other accompanying name to identify the signer. If the signer repeats the same noncompliant S-signature after being required to correct it, the reply will not be considered a bona fide attempt and no additional time will be given to submit a proper signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified documents required by statute must be originals
rubrics_metrics.description: When a document that is required by statute to be certified must be filed, a copy, including a photocopy or facsimile transmission, of the certification is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: certified copy of a foreign patent application under 35 U.S.C. 119 or certified copy of an international application under 35 U.S.C. 365 required by 37 CFR 1.55. Exception: priority documents retrieved by the Office under a PDX agreement can serve as the certified copy if 37 CFR 1.55(h) requirements are met. Certifications not provided for by statute (e.g., 37 CFR 1.8) do not require an original certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification cannot change signer name; name changes require rule-based request
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratification or confirmation alone does not provide a means for changing the name of a signer; a desired name change in an application must be by way of a request under 37 CFR 1.48(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: inventor wishing to change their name in a nonprovisional application must follow 37 CFR 1.48(f) procedures; ratification only addresses signature authenticity, not legal name changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality requirement for Internet use
rubrics_metrics.description: If security and confidentiality cannot be attained for a specific use, transaction, or activity, then that specific use, transaction, or activity shall NOT be undertaken/conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Internet use by Patent Organization employees, contractors, and consultants must ensure compliance with confidentiality requirements in statutes, including 35 U.S.C. 122. Where written authorization is given by applicant for USPTO to communicate via email, such communications may be used, but subject to other restrictions in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written authorization required for Internet/email communications containing confidential info
rubrics_metrics.description: Without a written authorization by applicant in place, the USPTO will not respond via email to any Internet correspondence which contains information subject to the confidentiality requirement as set forth in 35 U.S.C. 122.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A paper copy of such correspondence and response will be placed in the appropriate patent application file. The written authorization may be submitted via EFS, mail, or fax but not by email. The Office encourages use of Form PTO/SB/439 and submission on a separate paper to facilitate processing and avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on use of email for filings and signature-required papers
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to an Office action or a paper requiring a signature may NOT be communicated by applicant to the USPTO via email even if written authorization is on record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies and papers requiring a signature must be filed electronically using the USPTO patent electronic filing system or in paper. If a reply to an Office action is improperly submitted by email, the submission will not be accepted as an adequate reply to avoid abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 133 and 37 CFR 1.135; a copy will be placed in the application file with indication that the reply is NOT ENTERED.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO employees initiating email communications
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees are NOT permitted to initiate communications with applicants via email unless there is a written authorization of record in the patent application by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant has authorized Internet communications, USPTO employees may respond to email and initiate communications via email. For reissue applications and reexamination proceedings, written authorization is required before initiating email to applicants/patentees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of sender for Internet/email communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Email must be initiated by a registered practitioner, or an applicant in a pro se application, and sufficient information must be provided to show representative capacity in compliance with 37 CFR 1.34 (e.g., attorney registration number, docket number, patent application number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because spoofing is a known risk, Patent Organization users must verify identity before disclosing information, e.g., by checking Patent Data Portal or the application file to verify email address previously provided. Do not disclose information until identity is adequately verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on interview-like communications via email/instant messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Email and instant messaging shall NOT be used to conduct an exchange of communications similar to those exchanged during telephone or personal interviews unless a written authorization has been given to use Internet email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authorized, a paper copy of the email/instant messaging contents MUST be made and placed in the patent application file as required by the Federal Records Act. Video conferencing interviews are permitted only using USPTO-provided tools and links originating from USPTO personnel; applicant-provided links or non-USPTO tools are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of USPTO tools for Internet communications and video interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: All Internet communications between USPTO employees and applicants must be made using USPTO tools; USPTO video conferencing tools may be used to conduct examiner interviews but authorization by practitioner is required and links must originate from the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All interviews by video conference must originate from USPTO links provided by the examiner; links provided by the applicant from non-USPTO video conferencing tools are not acceptable. No personal phones, email, PDAs, etc. may be used by USPTO employees for Official communications. Practitioner participation in a video interview is considered consent to use the video conferencing tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backup, archiving, and recovery responsibility for Internet communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Backup, archiving, and recovery of information sent or received via the Internet is the responsibility of individual users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OCIO does not, and will not, as a normal practice, provide backup and recovery services for information produced, retrieved, stored, or transmitted to/from the Internet.
